Vanessa — quick proposal below, trying to keep simplicity for procurement. Numbers are uplift % on top of the base hosted rate (applies to consumption-based tokens/requests). We should surface both uplift % and an optional retainer so Brightline can pick which fits ops model.

Proposal (short):
- Continuity Gold — target: 99.99% uptime, critical response SLA: 30 minutes (24/7)
  - Uplift: +18% on base rate
  - Optional on-call retainer: $12,000/mo (includes two after-hours escalations per month; additional at $150/hr)
  - Pilot concession: first 30 days of pilot uplift waived (apply uplift from day 31)

- Continuity Silver — target: 99.95% uptime, response SLA: 2 hours (business hrs)
  - Uplift: +9% on base rate
  - No retainer required; after-hours billed at standard overtime rates

- Continuity Standard — target: 99.9% uptime, response SLA: 24 hours (business hrs)
  - Uplift: +3% on base rate
  - Included in standard contract (no retainer)

Discount / commit:
- 12-month committed ARR threshold: $150k —> up to 20% off list consumption pricing (applies before uplift).
- We can approve up to 18% discount without exec approval if contract value is > $250k ACV; otherwise need signoff from revenue ops.

Prorating: uplift is prorated daily for partial quarters; pilot waiver is prorated by day.

Operational notes: include an explicit failover runway in the SOW — a "regional fallback" policy that triggers when primary region latency > X for > 5 minutes; that will be covered under Gold and Silver but priced only under Gold for guaranteed warm standby capacity.

Margin check: with a 20% committed discount plus Gold uplift the blended margin compresses ~6–8 percentage points versus list — acceptable for strategic pilot but not at scale unless we negotiate steeper commit or exec-level concession.

If Kimberly/Marissa OK with the retainer numbers I can fold into the worksheet and produce a DocuSign summary.

-Jordan
VP, Solutions & Pricing | Redwood Inference
